name: Seattle
tax_rate: City special hotel-motel tax not imposed; 7% King County convention and trade center tax inside Seattle; 2.3% STIA fee at 71 downtown hotels
notes: No city LTAC grant program found; Seattle lodging taxes go to the Washington State Convention Center and the STIA fee goes to Visit Seattle marketing.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Tax Reference Manual: Convention Center Taxes
funding_docs.summary: Describes the King County convention and trade center tax (7% inside Seattle, 2.8% elsewhere in King County) that funds the Washington State Convention Center; this is where Seattle lodging tax goes rather than to a city grant program.

funding_docs.title: Hotel and Lodging Tax in Seattle 2026 (Roommaster summary)
funding_docs.summary: Secondary summary showing Seattle's combined 15.7% lodging rate, no city special hotel-motel tax imposed, and the 2.3% STIA fee at 71 downtown hotels that funds Visit Seattle marketing.

pool_note: No city lodging tax fund: the 7% convention center tax inside Seattle is a King County/state levy committed to Washington State Convention Center debt and the STIA fee goes to Visit Seattle, so nothing is open to outside applicants.

alternatives.program: Port of Seattle Tourism Marketing Support Program
alternatives.administrator: Port of Seattle Tourism Development
alternatives.funds: Matching (2:1) marketing grants, up to $20,000 (Tier 1) or $10,000 (Tier 2), from a roughly $600,000 annual pool, for projects that attract out-of-state visitors and promote SEA airport, cruise or marinas.
alternatives.eligibility: Washington cities, counties, DMOs, ports, chambers, tribal organizations and nonprofits; for-profit event producers must partner with an eligible applicant.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Annual RFP, historically released in winter with spring awards (2026-2027 cycle was posted on OMWBE); check the Port program page for the 2027-2028 window.
alternatives.contact: Not listed on the program page; contact Port of Seattle Tourism Development through portseattle.org
alternatives.notes: Regional alternative to the nonexistent Seattle LTAC; a nonprofit partner (e.g., a festival association) would need to be the applicant.

awards_history.typical_award: Tier 1 up to $20,000, Tier 2 up to $10,000, each with a 2:1 match (up to 50% of match may be administrative costs). $600,000 per two-year cycle; 2026-27: 35 awards, 24 at the $20,000 maximum, others $7,000-$12,500. Program runs on a two-year cycle (2024-25, 2026-27); next cycle expected to open late 2027/early 2028. Awards go to nonprofits, cities and DMOs marketing to out-of-state/fly-in visitors through SEA.

name: Bellevue
tax_rate: 5.5% city transient occupancy tax (grandfathered) plus $2.50/night TPA fee
notes: 100% of Bellevue's lodging tax passes to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority (Meydenbauer Center) under an agreement running to 2034, so there is no open LTAC application.

funding_docs.summary: States that 100% of Bellevue's transient occupancy (lodging) tax passes through to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority under an operating agreement running to 2034, paying Meydenbauer Center bonds, capital reinvestment and part of operations.

funding_docs.summary: City ordinance governing Bellevue's special hotel/motel tax; no outside grant process is created by it.

pool_note: Revenue figure not published; per the 2021-22 budget 100% of the city's lodging tax passes through to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority through 2034, leaving nothing for outside applicants.

alternatives.program: Bellevue Festivals & Events Incubator Program
alternatives.administrator: Visit Bellevue / Bellevue Tourism Promotion Area (with City of Bellevue)
alternatives.funds: Cash awards of $7,500 to $50,000 per event on a three-year funding cycle, tiered by attributable Bellevue hotel room nights (250-500 nights: $7,500-$15,000; 500-1,000: $15,000-$25,000; 1,000-3,000: $25,000-$50,000; 3,000+: $50,000). 60% paid on approval four months before the event, 40% after the final report.
alternatives.eligibility: Festivals and events held in Bellevue that can document hotel room nights; ranked higher if multi-day, weekend-heavy, out-of-region draw, in need months (Jan-Apr, Nov-Dec), and in a focus area (tech, wellness, culinary, multicultural, shopping, creative economy). No formal nonprofit requirement listed.
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis; decisions issued once per quarter, 90-120 days after applying. Apply at least 4-6 months before the event.
alternatives.contact: jkantor@visitbellevue.com; Visit Bellevue (877) 425-2075; 11100 NE 6th St, Bellevue, WA 98004
alternatives.notes: Best fit for a multi-night ticketed balloon glow; require Visit Bellevue logo, hotel room block promotion, attendee data collection and an economic impact report.

Program is a sponsorship/support model rather than a fixed-tier grant: every supported event must have a minimum hotel room block and a venue contract, with event-specific KPIs.

The Event Marketing and Sports Event Marketing categories first appear as separately pooled line items for the 2027 cycle (Event Marketing $42,950 pool; Sports Event Marketing $55,500 pool; scoring requires 300 peak / 500 total room nights for Event Marketing and 200 room nights per event for Sports). Per-organization amounts and the Impact Level A / Level B / Comprehensive split are not published in press releases, TCAB minutes, or guidelines; TCAB minutes (June 2, 2025) only confirm notifications went out. The 40 orgs listed are the first half (alphabetical) of the 80 funded for 2026-27; the other 40 are: Tacoma City Ballet, Tacoma Community Boat Builders, Tacoma Concert Band, Tacoma Fun Parade, Tacoma Historical Society, Tacoma Little Theatre, Tacoma Music Academy, Tacoma Music Collaborative, Tacoma Musical Playhouse, Tacoma Opera, Tacoma Photo Center, Tacoma Puzzle Hunt, Tacoma Refugee Choir, Tacoma Sister Cities, Tacoma Tree Foundation, Tacoma Youth Symphony Association, Tacoma Youth Theatre, Tahoma Indian Center, Ted Brown Music Outreach, The Grand Cinema, The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra, The Night Media Foundation, The Puget Sounds, Toolbox Learning Laboratories, Vision253, WayOut Kids, World Affairs Council of Tacoma, Write253, Mo' Motion Dance, Momentum Musician LLC, Northwest Repertory Singers, Oasis Youth Center, One Table Show, Pacific Northwest Dance Foundation, Queer NW, Remakery, Screaming Butterflies Theatre, Second Cycle Community Cycle Center, Southeast Asian Comedy Collective, Swan Creek Art Academy. Eligibility requires a Tacoma business address (limited Pierce County exception for orgs delivering 75%+ programming in Tacoma) and a primary purpose of arts, culture, heritage or science. Average award across all categories is roughly $80,000 but that is skewed by large Comprehensive awards to museums and theaters.

tax_rate: 4% total (2% basic plus 2% special per DOR Q2 2026 table; mayor's February 2026 memo cites 4% on hotels, motels, Airbnbs, RV parks)
deadline_pattern: Applications are reviewed in late summer and awards approved by City Council in October or November for the following year (council approved 2024 awards Nov 2023 and 2026 awards Oct 6, 2025); the mayor said Langley's allocation runs after Island County's and the program would be reviewed in the first quarter of 2026, so the 2027 cycle timing may change

annual_pool: $56,816 awarded for 2026 across 11 recipients (requests totaled $116,075); $98,100 awarded for 2024 from about $122,000 anticipated. A February 2026 proposal would dedicate 25% of current-year collections to the grant cycle and 25% to the Chamber visitor center contract
contact: City of Langley, Mayor Kennedy Horstman (langleywa.org; the city website could not be fetched for this entry, so no staff contact was confirmed)
notes: Langley disbanded its standing Lodging Tax Advisory Commission and now uses a temporary ad hoc committee (two lodging-tax collectors and two recipients) that scores applications on countywide benefit, shoulder-season focus, economic impact and regenerative tourism, then recommends awards to council. In February 2026 the mayor proposed reallocating lodging tax so that 12.5% goes to Island County joint tourism, 31.25% to city tourism facilities, 6.25% to affordable housing, and the remaining 50% split evenly between the grant cycle and the Chamber visitor center contract; the council also planned to review the whole program in early 2026 with three new councilmembers.

tax_rate: 4% total (2% basic plus 2% special per DOR Q2 2026 table); the town calls its program the '2 percent' lodging tax grant
deadline_pattern: Applications due to the Clerk-Treasurer at Town Hall by the last business day of September; scored applications discussed at the first council meeting in October and awards made by the second October meeting (policy adopted 2017, amended 2018)
typical_open: Late summer; forms available from Town Hall ahead of the end-of-September deadline
annual_pool: Roughly $25,000 to $50,000 a year depending on carryover: $33,250 awarded for 2019, $39,300 for 2022 (about $50,000 available), $49,000 for 2023 (drawing on about $64,000 accumulated during the pandemic)

notes: Coupeville is under 5,000 population so it has no statutory LTAC; the Town Council itself scores the applications using set criteria and makes the awards at its October meetings. Since 2017 any nonprofit may apply (the council replaced a fixed recipient list), with preference for activities inside town limits, shoulder-season (October to May) events, direct economic benefit and overnight stays, and projects that highlight local history, natural resources or traditions. The Chamber of Commerce visitor center ($20,000 to $26,000 a year), Musselfest marketing, the Island County Historical Museum and Tour de Whidbey are regular recipients and the town keeps a share for its own tourism activities.

meeting_schedule: No committee; Town Council handles 2% grants at its two regular October meetings each year

tax_rate: 2% state-shared basic lodging tax (DOR 2024 shows $219,868 state-shared, $0 special)
deadline_pattern: Applications open in early August and close in late August for the following calendar year (Aug 23, 2024 for 2025; Aug 24, 2026 for 2027); LTAC reviews in mid-to-late September and council approves in early October
typical_open: Early August (press release August 4, 2026 for the 2027 cycle)
annual_pool: 2026 cycle: $210,000 from the year's fund plus $84,000 from reserves, $294,000 total available; 2024 lodging tax distributions $219,868 (DOR)
contact: Jessica Bronstein, Executive/Legal Assistant, City Manager's Office, jbronstein@kelso.gov, 360-577-3379; 203 S. Pacific Ave, P.O. Box 819, Kelso, WA 98626
notes: Kelso runs a straightforward annual Lodging Tax Fund request through the City Manager's Office: packets go out in early August, proposals (original plus 5 copies) are due in late August, the Lodging Tax Advisory Committee reviews them at an open afternoon meeting in September, and council adopts the recommendations at its next meeting in early October. The 2026 round awarded $100,000 each to Tam O'Shanter Park and the Kelso Longview Chamber Visitor Information Center, $25,000 to the Kelso Highlander Festival, $11,500 to the Braided 64 wrestling tournament, $10,000 to S'quatchfest and $2,500 to Lights in the Park. Only public agencies and nonprofits may apply; priority goes to overnight stays in Kelso lodging, visitors from outside Cowlitz County, documented economic benefit and a track record. Funding is reimbursement-only under a Municipal Services Contract with insurance naming the city.

meeting_schedule: LTAC meets once a year in September to review applications (Sept 17, 2025; Sept 28, 2022); council acts at its next regular meeting in early October (Oct 7, 2025)
pool_note: 2026 cycle: $210,000 current-year fund plus $84,000 reserves = $294,000 available. $100,000 went to Tam O'Shanter Park, a city-owned park, leaving about $194,000 for outside applicants; the Chamber VIC takes $100,000 of that through the same application. notes: Sunnyside issues a formal Lodging Tax Funding RFP each summer; sealed proposals go to the Administrative Services Office, LTAC may ask for oral presentations, and recommendations go to council, which cannot fund anything LTAC did not recommend. For 2026 LTAC recommended $116,500 on November 13, 2025: Cinco de Mayo (Rotary) $30,000, Sunshine Days $20,000, Summer Ale Fest $15,000, Jerry Taylor Veterans Plaza $10,000, Lighted Farm Implement Parade $5,000, American Hill Climb $5,000 and a high school Show & Shine $1,500, while declining Miss Sunnyside and the Nitro Nationals as self-sustaining or off-mission. The committee wants proof of advertising beyond a 50-mile radius and 'heads in beds' growth before raising awards, favors October-April overnight stays, and reimburses only after receipts. For-profit businesses are explicitly eligible.

name: Twisp
tax_rate: Twisp Municipal Code 3.30 imposes two 2% lodging taxes (basic plus additional); in September 2025 the mayor described the rate as 2% and floated raising it to 4%; DOR 2024 shows $23,613 state-shared and $23,574 special
deadline_pattern: No application process; the town council allocates the fund directly during fall budget deliberations (September-December)
annual_pool: 2024 revenue $47,186; 2025 budgeted $42,000 against $68,539 in expenses; fund in deficit
contact: Town of Twisp, Mayor Hans Smith; Town Hall
notes: Twisp has no grant program and no LTAC (population under 5,000). The council spends the roughly $42,000-$47,000 a year directly: a contract with the Twisp Chamber of Commerce ($25,000 for 2026, down from $30,000, for Twispfest, Mistletoe Madness and the 4th of July parade), $2,000 to the Creative District, $1,000 to the Tree Board, and the largest line, about $16,000-plus for public restroom cleaning. Revenue fell 13% from 2021 to 2024 while expenses rose 35%, the fund is running a deficit, and in December 2025 the mayor told the Chamber not to count on lodging tax money in 2027. An outside event would have to be pitched to the council directly, and the money is not there; Okanogan County's LTAC is the realistic route.
meeting_schedule: No LTAC; Town Council meets the second and fourth Tuesdays at 5:30 p.m.
pool_note: 2024 revenue $47,186 (town packet; DOR agrees at $47,186). 2025 budget committed $25,000 Chamber, $2,000 Creative District, $1,000 Tree Board and about $40,000 for restrooms and facilities, exceeding revenue; nothing is set aside for outside applicants.

name: Milton
tax_rate: 2% lodging excise tax (Pierce County portion, RCW 67.28.180) and 2% special excise tax on lodging with 59 or fewer units in the King County portion (Milton Municipal Code 3.17); DOR location code 2709
notes: Milton Municipal Code chapter 3.17 levies the tax, creates a lodging tax fund and provides for a five-member LTAC (council chair, two lodging collectors, two recipients), but the city has almost no lodging: DOR Table L1 shows $2,033 distributed in 2024 and the city reported no spending to JLARC for 2022-2024. No LTAC roster, application or awards appear on cityofmilton.net. Milton is expressly within the Pierce County Lodging Tax Grant Program's eligible area, which is the real funding route.
pool_note: 2024 receipts of $2,033 per DOR Table L1; no grant pool.

name: South Cle Elum
tax_rate: 2% special hotel-motel tax, location code 1905 (DOR Q2 2026 lodging rate flyer)

Kittitas County's CLTAC program is a joint fund of the county and the cities of Cle Elum, Ellensburg and Roslyn; South Cle Elum is not a listed participant, so confirm with the County Auditor whether a South Cle Elum event (which draws county-wide overnight stays) can apply.

alternatives.program: Kittitas County Lodging Tax Fund (CLTAC) grants
alternatives.administrator: Kittitas County Auditor's Office (joint program of Kittitas County and the cities of Cle Elum, Ellensburg and Roslyn)
alternatives.funds: Pool not stated on the guide page; county distributions were $2,623,195 in 2024 (DOR Table L1); ongoing events capped at 10% of expense budget
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofits (501(c)(3), 501(c)(6)) and public entities for tourism marketing, events and festivals, and tourism facilities; South Cle Elum is not listed as a participating city, so confirm with the Auditor whether a South Cle Elum event qualifies (events are scored on county-wide tourism impact)
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Applications due mid-September (September 18, 2026, 4 pm) for the following year; workshops in mid-August; oral presentations to CLTAC in late November (November 20, 2026)
alternatives.notes: Minimum average score of 50 points; preference for projects that increase overnight stays and show a path to self-sustainability.
